rule.description: A function of the package embeds the significant implementation vocabulary of another still-available package function (attribute paths, call paths, non-local names, keyword-argument names and literal constants, function-local variables ignored, reusable scaffolding excluded), reproducing at least 55% of that helper's token multiset, at least half of its distinct tokens, at least 4 matched distinct tokens and at least 3 of its package-rare tokens, while being strictly larger than the helper.

checks.description: Detect functions that re-execute a copy of another available package function's implementation instead of invoking it.
checks.detected_relation: command/display function -> embedded implementation of a still-available helper function
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The calling function performs the lower-level work itself (environment staging, rc preparation, subprocess capture, column arithmetic, inventory derivation) that the package already factors into a reusable helper, duplicating that helper layer at the call site instead of delegating to it.

excluded.reason: Shares only argparse command scaffolding and one shared delegation with rename_cmd; the rule excludes scaffolding, so natural sibling similarity between commands is not treated as an embedded implementation.
Composes the creation path through the package helpers rather than re-executing their bodies; its shared tokens are scaffolding the rule deliberately ignores.
Pass-through command below the rule's minimum helper body (3 executable statements, 8 distinct tokens); trivial wrappers cannot carry an embedded implementation.
